section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you allowed to drive on the shoulder of the road?
options: a:Whenever you need to pass another vehicle.,b:When the car in front of you is turning.,c:When the car in front of you is driving too slowly.,d:Only when directed to do so by an official.
note: Driving on the shoulder is permitted only under official direction (e.g., emergency or traffic control); it is not a legal passing lane.

question: Roads are most slippery at which time?
options: a:When it has been raining hard for several hours.,b:When they are clean and dry.,c:During a heavy downpour after several hours.,d:Just after it starts to rain.
note: Road surface oils mix with the first rain, creating very slippery conditions often during the first half-hour of rain.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is correct?
options: a:You should use cruise control to maintain speed across tracks.,b:You have the right-of-way at all railroad crossings.,c:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger or stop sign.,d:You never need to stop at railroad crossings.
note: Stop at railroad crossings when signs, signals, or flaggers direct you to do so, and always proceed with caution near tracks.

question: If an overhead lane sign shows an arrow with the word 'ONLY' beneath it, what must you do?
options: a:Always change lanes to the left.,b:Drive in the direction shown by the arrow.,c:Look for a destination sign to decide.,d:Ignore the arrow if the way looks clear.
note: A lane control sign indicates you must travel in the direction shown by the arrow from that lane.

question: When roads are icy or snowy, what should you do before descending a steep hill?
options: a:Follow closely behind the vehicle ahead to maintain traction.,b:Pump the brakes continuously to prevent freezing.,c:Shift into a low gear before going down the hill.
note: On slippery slopes, shift to a low gear to use engine braking and avoid riding the brakes; maintain extra space behind the vehicle ahead and avoid quick stops. If you don’t have ABS, you may need to pump the brakes to slow down.

question: If your car's suspension is in poor condition, what problem can result?
options: a:Vehicle control problems.,b:Squealing brakes.,c:Improved fuel economy.,d:Increased tire pressure.
note: Bad suspension reduces vehicle control and ride comfort and may make the car difficult to handle.

question: How must you yield when an emergency vehicle with siren and lights approaches?
options: a:Stop immediately even if you are in an intersection.,b:Drive as close as possible to the right edge of the road and stop.,c:Move into the right lane and slow until it passes.
note: Pull to the right edge of the road and stop, avoiding stopping in an intersection, until the emergency vehicle passes.

question: When in rainy weather you should be most cautious when turning or stopping:
options: a:Only during heavy downpours.,b:When the pavement is freshly cleaned.,c:During the first half hour of rain.,d:After it has been raining hard for several hours.
note: Roads are especially slippery shortly after rain begins because oil and residue on the surface mix with the water.

question: What do signs with orange backgrounds indicate?
options: a:General warning signs.,b:Regulatory instructions.,c:Construction and maintenance warnings.
note: Orange signs are specifically used to warn drivers about construction and maintenance areas ahead.

question: If a child is about to run into the street, what should you do immediately?
options: a:Begin to prepare to slow down in stages.,b:Sound a sharp blast of your horn to warn them.,c:Flash your headlights to get attention.,d:Drive past slowly so as not to startle the child.
note: If a child or pedestrian is about to enter your path, a sharp horn blast can warn them and help prevent a collision.

question: During what times are drivers required to use headlights?
options: a:Only during the day in clear weather.,b:From one-half hour after sunset until one-half hour before sunrise,c:Whenever the driver feels tired.
note: Headlights are legally required from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise and anytime visibility drops below 200 feet.

question: What is the only thing that can lower your BAC and reduce alcohol’s effects?
options: a:Consuming coffee or caffeine.,b:Eating high-fat foods.,c:Taking a cold shower.,d:Time for the body to metabolize the alcohol.
note: Only the passage of time allows the body to remove alcohol; nothing else speeds up the process.

question: When is it acceptable to drive while using a medication that impairs your driving?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If you don't feel drowsy.,c:Only if it was prescribed by a physician.,d:If you take half the recommended dose.
note: It is illegal and unsafe to drive under the influence of any substance—alcohol, prescription or over-the-counter medications, or illegal drugs—that impairs your ability to drive.

question: When encountering a flashing yellow traffic signal at an intersection, how should you proceed?
options: a:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,b:Yield to all traffic before crossing regardless of conditions.,c:Stop first
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution—slow down and be alert for cross traffic or other hazards.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate about passing?
options: a:Passing is allowed from both directions.,b:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,c:Passing is allowed only from your direction of travel.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing for traffic in both directions.

question: When backing up a vehicle, what is the correct practice?
options: a:Use your side mirrors only.,b:Look through the rear window while backing up.,c:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,d:Press the accelerator as needed to move quickly.
note: When reversing, turn and look through the rear window; do not depend solely on mirrors and move at a low speed.

question: If your vehicle's rear end skids to the left, what steering action should you take?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel straight and speed up.,b:Steer to the right.,c:Tap the brakes lightly and shift into neutral.,d:Steer to the left (in the direction you want to go).
note: If your rear skids left, steer left to bring the front of the vehicle into alignment with the rear; avoid braking hard during the skid.

question: When preparing to exit an interstate, when should you begin slowing?
options: a:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,b:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.,c:As you approach the deceleration lane.
note: Maintain highway speed until in the deceleration lane, then reduce speed to the advisory exit speed before the ramp curve.

question: South Dakota requires vehicles to be covered by liability insurance:
options: a:Only when driven by a minor.,b:Only when registered out of state.,c:Only when used on an interstate.,d:At all times.
note: State law requires vehicles to be properly registered and insured at all times; drivers must carry proof of insurance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may drivers stop in a travel lane?
options: a:Never.,b:When dropping off a passenger.,c:When they are lost.
note: Do not stop in travel lanes for any reason; pull completely off the roadway when stopping is necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, what is your responsibility regarding oncoming traffic and pedestrians?
options: a:Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before completing the turn.,b:Only yield if the light is red.,c:They must yield to you when you have a turn signal.,d:Proceed because turning vehicles have priority.
note: When making a left turn, yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians who have the right-of-way until it is safe to turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what condition is it legal to turn left on a red light after stopping?
options: a:Only if a police officer directs you to do so.,b:Only when you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street and no signs prohibit it.,c:When you are on a two-way street turning onto a two-way street.,d:Whenever you yield to all other traffic.
note: Left turns on red are permitted only from a one-way street onto another one-way street after a complete stop and when not prohibited by signs.

question: Why should you avoid using high beam headlights in fog or mist?
options: a:Approaching vehicles might not see you as well.,b:High beams will reflect back into your eyes and reduce visibility.,c:Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.
note: High beams reflect off fog, rain, or snow and create glare that reduces visibility; use low beams instead.

question: At dawn, dusk, and in rain or snow, what should you turn on to be better seen?
options: a:Your parking lights.,b:Your headlights.,c:Your interior dome light.,d:Your instrument panel lighting.
note: Use headlights whenever visibility is reduced so other drivers can see your vehicle; low beams are usually appropriate.

question: If it feels like your tires have lost contact with the road surface, what action should you take?
options: a:Pump the brakes rapidly to regain control.,b:Turn the steering wheel sharply away from the skid.,c:Ease your foot off the gas and avoid braking until traction returns.,d:Shift to a lower gear to slow quickly.
note: If you suspect loss of contact (hydroplaning), release the accelerator and avoid braking or turning abruptly until tires regain traction.

question: Where are high beam headlights appropriate to use?
options: a:Both of the above.,b:Whenever there may be pedestrians anywhere around.,c:On unfamiliar roads or where there are no oncoming vehicles
note: Use high beams to increase visibility where there are no nearby vehicles; switch to low beams when another vehicle approaches.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers making left turns must yield to:
options: a:No one in particular.,b:Passing cars only.,c:Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.
note: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic (including bicycles and motorcycles) that is going straight or turning right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive faster than surrounding traffic and keep passing on a two-lane road, what is the likely result?
options: a:Reduce fuel consumption for all drivers.,b:Help prevent traffic congestion.,c:Increase your chances of a collision.,d:Get you to your destination much more quickly and safely.
note: Repeated passing on two-lane roads raises the odds of a collision each time you pass another vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If there is no marked crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.,b:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.,c:Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.
note: Even without a marked crosswalk, drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing their lane and allow them to finish crossing.

question: To check blind spots before changing lanes, which method should you use?
options: a:Use only the outside mirror on the side you’re moving toward.,b:Rely only on the inside rearview mirror.,c:Look over your shoulder toward the blind spot.,d:Signal and assume the lane is clear.
note: Blind spots are not visible in mirrors; turn your head and look over your shoulder to check the area before changing lanes.

question: How can you check for vehicles in your blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Check the inside rearview mirror only.,b:Rely only on the outside mirrors.,c:Use the turn signal without looking.,d:Look over your left or right shoulder toward the area you cannot see in the mirrors.
note: Blind spots are not visible in mirrors; look over the appropriate shoulder to verify the lane is clear before changing.

question: When you see an octagonal traffic sign approaching an intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and yield as required.,b:Turn right immediately.,c:Ignore it if no other cars are present.,d:Slow down but you do not need to stop.
note: An octagonal sign always means STOP. You must stop fully, yield to traffic and pedestrians with the right-of-way, and proceed only when safe.

question: If an oncoming vehicle doesn't dim its high beams at night, what is the best action?
options: a:Look straight ahead in your lane.,b:Look toward the left edge of the lane.,c:Look toward the right edge of your lane and use peripheral vision.
note: Avoid looking directly at blinding headlights; glance toward the right side of your lane and watch the road from the corner of your eye.

question: If you are on a city street and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Stay in your lane and slow down until it passes.,b:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,c:Drive to the right edge and slow down but not stop.
note: You must pull to the right edge of the roadway and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless you are in an intersection; then proceed through and stop.

question: What are the consequences of refusing an alcohol analysis test when requested by law enforcement in South Dakota?
options: a:You have the right to refuse with no consequences.,b:Your driver's license will be suspended.,c:You will be fined but face no license action.,d:You will be allowed to take the test later without penalty.
note: Implicit consent laws mean refusal to submit to a requested alcohol or drug test results in administrative license suspension.

question: Before starting the engine, what should you do regarding seat belts?
options: a:Buckle your safety belt and ensure passengers are buckled.,b:Buckle only if you are driving at highway speeds.,c:Tell passengers to buckle after you start driving.,d:Put on the belt after the engine is running.
note: Make a habit of fastening your seat belt and confirming passengers are buckled before switching on the ignition.

question: Which of the following is a safe driving habit?
options: a:Staring constantly at the road ahead without scanning.,b:Using high beam headlights in fog for better visibility.,c:Keeping both hands off the wheel when cruising.,d:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently to stay aware.
note: Regularly scan mirrors and the road to detect hazards; use low beams in fog, not high beams.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street, where should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Near the centerline (in the lane closest to the center).,b:Near the right-hand side of the road.,c:On the left of the centerline.,d:In the right-turn-only lane.
note: Begin the left turn from the lane nearest the centerline and turn into the first available legal lane without cutting the corner.

question: How should you treat an intersection with a flashing yellow traffic signal?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution after checking for hazards.,b:Come to a full stop then proceed, as with a stop sign.,c:Wait for a green light before moving.,d:Ignore it unless pedestrians are present.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow down, be alert, and proceed cautiously through the intersection.

question: When another driver is tailgating you, what should you do regarding the space in front of your vehicle?
options: a:Brake sharply to teach them a lesson.,b:Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.,c:Flash your brakes to warn the tailgater.,d:Create extra space ahead of your vehicle to reduce sudden braking risk.
note: When being tailgated, leave extra room in front of your vehicle and avoid sudden braking. Gradually slow down or change lanes when safe so the tailgating driver can pass.

question: Which is a common consequence of excessive speed?
options: a:It improves your ability to react to hazards.,b:It does not affect crash chances.,c:It often leads to high-risk decision-making and increases crash likelihood.
note: Excessive speed reduces reaction time and increases the severity and likelihood of crashes due to riskier decisions.

question: If your vehicle’s wheels have left the paved road onto the shoulder, what is the correct immediate response?
options: a:Turn sharply back onto the pavement immediately.,b:Hold the wheel steady,c:Apply full brakes and jerk the wheel to the left.,d:Speed up to try to get back on the pavement quickly.
note: If you run off the pavement, release the gas, hold the steering wheel firmly, and slow down gradually before steering back onto the road when safe.

question: If a vehicle is equipped with airbags, what should you still do?
options: a:Rely on the airbag and skip the belt.,b:Wear the seat belt behind your back.,c:Always wear your seat belt.,d:Disable the airbag to avoid injury.
note: Airbags supplement seat belts; for best protection, always use the lap and shoulder belts in combination with airbags.

question: What are blind spots?
options: a:Areas that cannot be seen in a vehicle’s mirrors.,b:Spots in your vision when you are tired.,c:Traffic control devices.
note: Blind spots are regions around your vehicle not visible in mirrors; always check over your shoulder before changing lanes.

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:
options: a:Change lanes at full speed.,b:Slow down because the lane ends ahead always.,c:Be prepared for workers and equipment and slow down.
note: Orange signs warn of construction; reduce speed and be prepared for workers, equipment, or lane shifts ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road, what should you do first?
options: a:Flash your headlights to signal the other driver.,b:Sound your horn as you pass.,c:Judge the distance and speed of any oncoming vehicles.
note: Ensure there is ample time and space to pass by judging the distance and speed of oncoming traffic before you move out to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What important action should you take before making a turn?
options: a:Increase your speed to complete the turn faster.,b:Always move to the left lane before turning.,c:Check traffic in all directions.
note: Before turning, check mirrors and look to the front, rear, and both sides to ensure turning can be done safely.

question: When you see a reflective orange triangle on a vehicle's rear, it means:
options: a:The vehicle is slow-moving (usually 25 mph or less).,b:The vehicle is an ambulance.,c:The vehicle is a school bus.
note: A reflective orange triangle marks slow-moving vehicles like farm equipment, indicating speeds typically of 25 mph or less.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How is a crosswalk defined?
options: a:A name for a four-way intersection.,b:The area where pedestrians are allowed to cross the roadway.,c:An area set aside for road workers.,d:A place where vehicles always have the right-of-way.
note: A crosswalk is the portion of the roadway designated for pedestrians to cross; it may be marked or unmarked and is protected by traffic laws.

question: A long truck turning right may appear to do what on a two-lane street?
options: a:Complete the turn strictly within the right lane.,b:Finish the turn in either of the two available lanes without swing.,c:Swing wide to complete the turn.
note: Large vehicles often need to swing wide when turning to accommodate their length and wheel paths.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Toward the edge of the road (right) so the vehicle will roll away from the center.,b:Straight ahead so it won’t roll.,c:Toward the center of the road (left) so it will roll into traffic.,d:Any direction is acceptable as long as you set the parking brake.
note: When parking uphill without a curb, turn wheels toward the road edge so the vehicle would roll away from the center if the brakes fail.

question: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle with lights and siren is approaching, what must you do?
options: a:Pull to the right of the intersection and stop immediately.,b:Continue through the intersection,c:Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
note: If already in the intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches, clear the intersection and then pull to the right and stop to yield the right-of-way.

question: If you intend to pass a pedestrian and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Honk to warn the pedestrian to move over.,b:Keep your speed and pass the pedestrian quickly.,c:Slow down and allow the oncoming vehicle to pass first.
note: When facing multiple hazards, let one threat clear first; slow and let the oncoming vehicle pass before passing the pedestrian.

question: What is the effect of slowing down just to look at collisions or unusual events?
options: a:It causes traffic congestion and can lead to further collisions.,b:It improves traffic flow by reducing speed variability.,c:It prevents rear-end collisions by encouraging slower traffic.,d:It is required by law to slow and observe.
note: Rubbernecking" slows traffic and increases the risk of secondary collisions; keep moving safely and avoid distractions."

question: Why is extra space needed in front of a large truck?
options: a:Because trucks always drive slower than cars.,b:To allow other drivers to merge in front of the truck.,c:So the truck has room to stop safely.,d:To give the truck room to turn more easily.
note: Large trucks require more stopping distance than cars; do not cut in front of a truck and then slow down suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal at an intersection turns steady yellow before you reach it, what should you do if you haven't entered the intersection?
options: a:Speed up to clear the intersection before it turns red.,b:Proceed through at the same speed.,c:Come to a safe stop.
note: A steady yellow warns that the light is about to turn red; if you haven't entered the intersection, you should safely stop.

question: What is a good way to avoid skidding on slick surfaces?
options: a:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.,b:Speed up before entering a curve and slow down exiting it.,c:Shift into a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
note: Reduce speed prior to curves or intersections to avoid braking or steering sharply on slippery surfaces which can cause skids.

question: After stopping for a train at a railroad crossing and the train passes, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Wait until the signal lights stop flashing.,b:Proceed immediately when the train has passed if the track looks clear.,c:Roll forward slowly to check for tracks.,d:Both wait for the signals to stop and look for a second train.
note: There may be more than one track; do not proceed until all gates are lifted and all warning signals have stopped flashing, and check for a second train.

question: If the centerline has one solid yellow and one broken yellow line next to your lane, what does that mean?
options: a:You are not allowed to pass here.,b:You are in a passing zone and may pass on the left when clear.,c:You may only make right turns here.
note: When the broken line is on your side, you may cross the centerline to pass if it’s safe; traffic on the solid-line side may not pass.

question: As your speed increases, what becomes more important?
options: a:Turning on headlights.,b:Changing lanes frequently to keep flow.,c:Looking well ahead of your vehicle.
note: At higher speeds your stopping distance increases, so scanning far ahead gives more time to react to hazards.

question: Before returning to your lane after overtaking another vehicle, what should you confirm?
options: a:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:You have flashed your headlights.,c:You are travelling at the same speed as before the pass.,d:You have sounded your horn to signal your return.
note: Only return when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror, indicating sufficient space.

question: Which road surface tends to freeze first?
options: a:A bridge,b:A tunnel,c:An intersection
note: Bridges and overpasses freeze before the surrounding roadway because air circulates above and below the pavement.

question: Which action helps reduce incidents of road rage?
options: a:Talk on your cell phone to stay calm.,b:Use your horn frequently to motivate other drivers.,c:Tailgate slower drivers to express frustration.,d:Always signal before changing lanes.
note: Signaling your intentions gives other drivers time to react and helps prevent conflicts that can lead to road rage.

question: Which headlights should you use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Hazard flashers only.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.,d:Low beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog; high beams reflect and reduce visibility for you and others.

question: Where is the safest place for children aged 12 and under to ride in a vehicle with airbags?
options: a:In the bed of a pickup truck.,b:In the front seat.,c:In the back seat.
note: Children 12 and under are safest in the rear seat because airbags can cause serious injury to young passengers in a crash.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.,b:Grip the wheel firmly,c:Brake as hard as you can immediately.
note: Hold the steering wheel steady, take your foot off the gas, and allow the vehicle to slow before braking gently if necessary, then pull off safely.

question: What should you do if the road is wet or icy?
options: a:Reduce your speed to improve traction.,b:Drive at the posted speed limit regardless.,c:Turn off your headlights to reduce glare.,d:Increase your speed to get through the hazard quickly.
note: On wet, snowy, or icy roads, reduce speed because tires have less traction than on dry pavement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:Blind spots can be seen using only the rearview mirror.,b:Blind spots are eliminated if you have one outside mirror.,c:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
note: Even with proper mirrors, blind spots remain; large trucks have especially extensive blind areas that other drivers should avoid.

question: Double solid yellow centerlines indicate that passing is:
options: a:Not allowed from either direction.,b:Allowed only from your direction of travel.,c:Allowed from both directions.,d:Allowed only during daylight hours.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean no vehicle from either direction may cross the lines to pass.

question: When approaching a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, what must you do?
options: a:Carefully drive around them.,b:Honk your horn to warn them as you pass.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the person is clear of your path.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog and not proceed until they are clear of your path.

question: Accumulating how many points on your driving record within 24 months will lead to license suspension in South Dakota?
options: a:15 points,b:30 points,c:22 points
note: In South Dakota, accruing 22 or more points within a 24-month period will result in suspension of your driver's license; suspension length varies by offenses.

question: When merging onto a freeway, at what speed should you enter traffic?
options: a:Enter at or near the speed of freeway traffic.,b:Enter five to ten mph slower than freeway traffic.,c:Enter at the posted speed limit regardless of traffic flow.
note: When merging, accelerate on the ramp so you can match the speed of vehicles on the freeway and merge safely. Entering too slowly can create a hazard.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only when the guide dog is actively leading them across the street.,b:Only if a crossing guard is present.,c:At all times.
note: Pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog must be given the right-of-way at all times when crossing.

question: How can you best monitor traffic behind your vehicle?
options: a:Rely only on side mirrors.,b:Turn and look out your back window periodically.,c:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,d:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots at all times.
note: Check your rearview mirror often to stay aware of traffic behind you and be prepared for changing conditions.

question: Which habit is especially dangerous in work zones?
options: a:Both of the above.,b:Failing to watch for workers and moving equipment.,c:Tailgating another vehicle.
note: Both tailgating and failing to watch for workers and machinery are dangerous in work zones; drive attentively and reduce speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the interstate, after matching the speed of traffic and signaling, what should you do?
options: a:Stop on the ramp until a vehicle makes room.,b:Merge carefully into the gap.,c:Wait for the lane to clear completely before merging.,d:Expect traffic to allow you to proceed because you have the right-of-way.
note: Identify a gap, accelerate to match traffic speed, signal, and merge into the gap when it is safe. Do not assume others will yield for you.

question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, what is a safe practice?
options: a:Follow closely to reduce wind drag.,b:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.,c:Avoid driving alongside it for long stretches because of its large blind spots.
note: Large trucks have big blind spots; avoid driving beside them for extended periods to maintain visibility and safety.

question: When a car with bright headlights approaches you at night, how should you respond?
options: a:Stop until the other driver passes.,b:Flash your high beams at them.,c:Glance toward the right edge of your lane to avoid being blinded.,d:Look directly at their headlights to judge distance.
note: Avoid looking directly at bright oncoming headlights; look toward the right edge of the road until the vehicle has passed.

question: What is the purpose of broken yellow lines on streets and highways?
options: a:Indicate no passing zones.,b:Separate lanes moving in the same direction.,c:Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions and allow passing.
note: Yellow lines divide opposite-direction traffic; dashed (broken) yellow lines mean passing is permitted when it’s safe.

question: What should you do to reduce traction loss on wet roads?
options: a:Turn off electronic stability control.,b:Slow down and avoid abrupt turns or braking.,c:Make sharp turns to maintain control.,d:Apply brakes firmly at the first sign of sliding.
note: To avoid hydroplaning and traction loss, reduce speed and avoid abrupt steering or braking on wet surfaces.

question: When is a collision more likely to occur relative to traffic flow?
options: a:When all vehicles travel at similar speeds.,b:When one lane is slightly faster than another.,c:When one vehicle is traveling significantly faster or slower than the flow.
note: Collisions are more likely when a vehicle's speed differs markedly from surrounding traffic, increasing chances of unsafe passing or rear-end crashes.

question: Which is the correct behavior when driving through a work zone?
options: a:Maintain your normal speed the whole way through.,b:Weave between cones to get ahead of traffic.,c:Increase speed to clear the zone quickly.,d:Reduce speed
note: Drive cautiously in work zones: slow down, follow posted limits, and watch for workers and equipment.

question: What does a yellow left-turn arrow in a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:Drivers should prepare to yield only to oncoming traffic.,b:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,c:The protected left-turn phase is ending and you must prepare to yield.
note: A yellow left arrow means the protected turn is ending; you should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic if you have not completed your turn.

question: What are "no zones" around large trucks?
options: a:Only the space directly behind the truck.,b:Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are so close they restrict the truck's ability to stop or maneuver.,c:Designated safe passing zones.,d:Areas where cars have several car lengths between their vehicle and the truck.
note: No zones are blind spots and danger areas around trucks where a car can be hidden from the truck driver or limit the truck driver's maneuverability.

question: Interstate driving requires drivers to:
options: a:Only be able to drive at higher speeds.,b:Relax because highways are safer.,c:Be constantly alert and have the ability to safely drive at increased speeds.
note: Driving on interstates requires alertness and the skill to operate your vehicle safely at higher speeds and in heavier traffic.

question: Before changing lanes, besides checking mirrors, what else should you do?
options: a:Never look over your right shoulder.,b:Glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,c:Always slow down in your lane.,d:Honk to let others know you are moving.
note: Check mirrors and glance over your shoulder to ensure the blind spot is clear before changing lanes.

question: What does a solid yellow line beside a broken yellow line mean for drivers next to the broken line?
options: a:Traffic next to the solid line may pass when safe.,b:Both directions may pass.,c:Traffic next to the broken line may pass when safe.,d:Neither direction may pass.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means drivers next to the broken line may cross to pass; drivers next to the solid line may not.

question: If you see pedestrians in an upcoming crosswalk, what should you do?
options: a:Continue ahead because you have the right-of-way.,b:Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.,c:Sound your horn and proceed quickly.,d:Wait for the pedestrians to finish crossing.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk and wait until the intersection is clear before proceeding.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Drink something with caffeine and keep going.,b:Stop and either rest or switch drivers.,c:Reduce speed and continue driving.,d:Open a window for fresh air.
note: To avoid drowsy driving, take breaks every hour or so on long trips or share driving so each person can sleep while the other drives.

question: When is it necessary to use low beam headlights?
options: a:Any time you are in fog.,b:Only when parked at night.,c:Only on a lighted street.,d:Only on a freeway.
note: Use low beams in fog, rain, snow, or mist because high beams can reflect off precipitation and reduce visibility.

question: If someone is tailgating you on a two-lane road and there's no lane to move into, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down gradually to encourage the tailgater to pass.,b:Speed up to increase distance from them.,c:Apply your brakes sharply to warn them.
note: If you cannot change lanes, gently reduce speed when safe to do so; this typically encourages a tailgater to pass or create space.

question: Which behavior most blocks smooth traffic flow?
options: a:Using public transportation instead of driving.,b:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,c:Slowing down to look at a collision scene (rubbernecking).,d:Signaling every lane change.
note: Rubbernecking causes slowdowns and contributes to congestion and secondary crashes; keep moving and stay focused on driving.

question: Why should you keep your turn signal on continuously while you are turning?
options: a:Signal continuously so other road users know your intentions.,b:Turning signals are only necessary when changing lanes.,c:Keeping it on makes the turn faster.,d:Because it's illegal to switch off your signal before completing the turn.
note: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing, or stopping so other drivers, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians understand your intentions.

question: Accumulating how many points on your license within 12 months can result in suspension in South Dakota?
options: a:Ten points.,b:Eight points.,c:Fifteen points.
note: In South Dakota, accumulating 15 or more points within a 12-month period can lead to license suspension; penalties vary by offense count.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you plan to pass another vehicle, which assumption is unsafe?
options: a:Not assuming the other driver will make space for you to return.,b:Assuming other drivers will maintain a constant speed.,c:Assuming the other driver will make room for you because you signaled.
note: Never assume other drivers will yield or make extra space just because you signal; always confirm it's safe before passing.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, how much space should you maintain?
options: a:More distance than you would behind a passenger vehicle.,b:Directly beside the truck to pass quicker.,c:As close as possible to use their slipstream.,d:One car length behind so the truck driver can see you.
note: Leave extra following distance behind large trucks so you can see around them and they have room to stop.

question: When following a motorcycle, you should:
options: a:Be ready to use your horn.,b:Allow a larger following distance.,c:Share the lane with the motorcycle.,d:Drive more slowly directly behind the motorcycle.
note: Maintain at least a three- to four-second following distance behind motorcycles because they can stop or swerve quickly.

question: You are exiting the freeway on a downhill ramp that curves. What should you do?
options: a:Wait until you are in the curve to begin braking.,b:Slow to the posted speed limit of the freeway first.,c:Slow to a safe speed before entering the curve.
note: Reduce speed before entering the curve; braking in a curve can cause skidding and loss of control.

question: If the driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk, what should you do?
options: a:Cautiously pass the vehicle at 10 mph or slower.,b:Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed before proceeding.,c:Change lanes and pass the stopped vehicle.,d:Sound your horn to make the driver move on.
note: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk; pedestrians may be crossing that you cannot see.

question: How should you adjust speed and steering when driving on snowy or icy roads?
options: a:Brake suddenly to test traction.,b:Drive the same as under normal conditions.,c:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,d:Make speed and directional changes more gradually than usual.
note: On snow or ice, make gradual speed and steering changes. Do not use cruise control because loss of traction can cause loss of control.

question: What are the standard colors for temporary construction or maintenance signs?
options: a:White background with red letters.,b:Orange background with black letters or symbols.,c:Red background with green letters.,d:Yellow background with blue letters.
note: Work zone and construction signs are orange with black writing and/or symbols to warn drivers of changed conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which passing actions are unlawful?
options: a:Passing on the right when multiple lanes are present.,b:Passing only on hills and curves when visibility is clear.,c:Passing in any marked no-passing zone or over a railroad crossing.,d:Passing during daylight in rural areas.
note: It is illegal to pass in marked no-passing zones, at railroad crossings, on hills or curves where visibility is limited, and where solid lines indicate no passing.

question: While driving at night, what should you do to compensate for reduced visibility?
options: a:Look directly into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.,b:Always use your high beams.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: At night increase following distance to give more reaction time; use lights correctly and avoid staring at oncoming headlights.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what is the correct action?
options: a:Brake hard and steer to the right edge of the roadway.,b:Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.,c:Pump the brakes rapidly to stop quickly.
note: If a blowout occurs, hold the wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, slow gradually, and move out of traffic when it is safe to do so; lightly apply brakes when needed.

question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?
options: a:Large trucks always travel faster than small vehicles.,b:Trucks can brake quicker due to advanced braking systems.,c:Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.,d:Drivers of small cars can’t see trucks in their mirrors.
note: Because of their size and weight, large vehicles require much longer stopping distances; sudden stops in front of them can lead to collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian who begins crossing after the 'Don't Walk' signal is flashing is mid-crossing when your light turns green. What must you do?
options: a:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.,b:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,c:Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing before proceeding.
note: You must yield to any pedestrian already in the crosswalk; wait for them to clear the roadway before moving on your green.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop at the intersection.,c:Accelerate to get through quickly.,d:Maintain your normal speed.
note: A flashing yellow signal warns to proceed with caution; slow down and be alert for other vehicles and pedestrians.

question: Which statement best describes how defensive drivers think?
options: a:They consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.,b:They assume other drivers will always do the right thing.,c:They expect no breaks and give none.,d:They rely solely on traffic signals for safety.
note: Defensive driving means anticipating potential mistakes by others and being ready to respond to avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic but your light is green, what should you do?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.,b:Follow other vehicles into the intersection so you don't delay.,c:Turn left to find an alternate route immediately.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely; entering and blocking it can result in a citation and impede traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is the correct method for checking blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.,b:You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder for all lane changes.,c:Vehicles with two outside mirrors do not have blind spots.
note: Signal, check mirrors, and look over the appropriate shoulder to ensure there is no vehicle in your blind spot before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers turning left must yield to which vehicles?
options: a:No one; they have the right-of-way.,b:Only pedestrians.,c:Vehicles overtaking from behind.,d:Oncoming cars.
note: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or otherwise has the right-of-way.

question: A broken yellow centerline next to your lane means what?
options: a:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is not permitted.,c:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow line on your side of the center indicates you may cross to pass when safe and there is no oncoming traffic.

question: What is the purpose of barriers, drums, cones, and signs in work zones?
options: a:To inconvenience drivers and slow traffic intentionally.,b:To provide decorative separation only.,c:To keep traffic out of hazardous areas and direct travel safely.,d:To make drivers angry about slowdowns.
note: Work zone devices warn drivers, channel traffic, and protect workers by keeping vehicles out of hazardous areas.

question: What is a common effect of continuous hard braking on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:It increases tire traction on ice.,b:It helps you stop faster in slippery conditions.,c:It often locks the front wheels,d:It keeps your brakes from freezing.
note: Continuous hard braking on ice or snow can lock the brakes and cause a loss of steering control; slow down and maintain a safe speed to reduce the need for heavy braking.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly swerve into the next lane.,b:Speed up to scare them away.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.,d:Stop and get out of your vehicle to move them.
note: Animals may bolt or travel in groups, so slow down and proceed cautiously—there may be more animals out of sight.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is the correct action to take?
options: a:Ease off the gas and steer in the direction of the skid.,b:Accelerate to regain traction.,c:Turn off the ignition immediately.,d:Brake as hard as possible.
note: Release the accelerator or brake and steer in the direction of the skid to help regain vehicle control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately and reverse to the exit.,b:Back up on the shoulder to reach the exit.,c:Cross the median to return to your exit.,d:Continue to the next exit and re-route; do not back up.
note: If you miss an exit, proceed to the next one and return via surface roads; never back up on the roadway or shoulder.

question: If you damage a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Call your insurance company when you get home without leaving a note.,b:Drive away and report it later to the police.,c:Leave a note with your name,d:Wait by the car until the owner returns.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle or property and cannot locate the owner, leave a note with your contact information and attempt to report the incident.

question: What can happen if you take a prescription drug and drink alcohol?
options: a:It will improve alertness.,b:It will likely have no effect.,c:It can make you unfit to drive.
note: Mixing alcohol with prescription or over-the-counter medications can intensify impairment and make you unsafe to drive.

question: What should you remove from your vehicle before driving in winter conditions?
options: a:Only the windshield and passenger window.,b:Only the front windshield so you can see ahead.,c:Just clear the headlights and taillights.,d:All snow
note: Clear all windows and mirrors of snow, ice, and frost so you have full visibility before driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Whose directions must drivers obey at construction sites?
options: a:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,b:Bystanders waving their hands.,c:Drivers with broken-down vehicles asking you to stop.,d:Flaggers (signal persons) directing traffic.
note: Flaggers are authorized to direct traffic in work zones and their instructions must be followed to protect workers and drivers.

question: If driving next to a single broken white line on a highway, what may you do?
options: a:You may cross only if you are in the left lane.,b:You cannot cross the line to pass.,c:You may cross the line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes going the same direction and allow lane changes and passing when safe.

question: When entering or exiting a driveway, what should drivers do regarding pedestrians?
options: a:Honk at pedestrians to make them yield.,b:Proceed without stopping if no vehicle is approaching.,c:Have the right-of-way over pedestrians.,d:Yield to pedestrians and stop before entering the sidewalk area.
note: Drivers leaving or entering driveways must yield to pedestrians using the sidewalk and stop before driving onto the sidewalk area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it legal to pass another vehicle?
options: a:On a curve if no oncoming vehicles are visible.,b:In any lane if traffic ahead is slow.,c:Only where signs or pavement markings allow overtaking.,d:Within an intersection if you don’t see oncoming traffic.
note: You may pass only where signs and pavement markings permit and only when you have enough space and visibility to do so safely.

question: What do double solid yellow lane markings mean?
options: a:The lane to the right may pass.,b:Both directions may pass when clear.,c:Neither direction may pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposite-direction traffic and prohibit passing from either direction.

question: At a red traffic light with a green arrow, when may you proceed in the arrow's direction?
options: a:Only after coming to a complete stop first.,b:Only if no other vehicles are present.,c:When you are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.,d:Only after the arrow turns off.
note: If a green arrow is displayed for your lane, you may turn in the arrow’s direction when the way is clear; you do not need to stop first.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving a distraction?
options: a:It occupies the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.,b:It causes the driver to worry about call costs.,c:It draws other drivers’ attention away from the road.
note: Cell phone use diverts your hands, eyes, and attention from driving, increasing crash risk even if you are experienced.

question: If the rear of your vehicle begins skidding left, how should you steer?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel left in the direction of the skid.,b:Brake hard immediately.,c:Do not turn the steering wheel at all.,d:Turn sharply right to counter the skid.
note: When skidding, take your foot off the accelerator, avoid braking, and steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline indicates what?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Do not pass.,c:Traffic light ahead.,d:Pass only during daylight hours.
note: A solid yellow line on your side means passing is prohibited; when adjacent to a broken yellow line, only the side with the broken line may pass.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what is the recommended initial response?
options: a:Pump the brakes repeatedly.,b:Brake abruptly to stop the skid.,c:Stay off the brakes and steer to regain control.
note: When a vehicle skids, avoid braking which can worsen the skid; steer smoothly to regain traction and control.

question: If weather or light conditions require headlights, which should you use?
options: a:Emergency flashers only.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.,d:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beams in poor visibility conditions; high beams will reflect and reduce forward visibility.

question: Who may legally use designated handicap parking spaces?
options: a:Anyone if all other spaces are full.,b:People who feel unwell even without a placard.,c:Delivery drivers unloading packages temporarily.,d:Only drivers with the appropriate license plate or hang tag.
note: Handicap spaces are reserved for persons with disabilities who display the proper plate or hang tag as defined by state law.

question: What is distracted driving?
options: a:Only using a cellphone while driving.,b:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.,d:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
note: Distracted driving includes any activity that diverts eyes, hands, or mind from driving and is a leading factor in crashes.

question: When parking on any hill, what should you always do?
options: a:Have one rear wheel touch the curb.,b:Keep your front wheels parallel to the road even if there's no curb.,c:Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park or in gear.
note: Always set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in park (or in gear for manual) when parked on a hill to prevent rolling.

question: When you encounter a flashing red traffic light, you must:
options: a:Proceed only after it turns green.,b:Treat the intersection as if it were controlled by a stop sign.,c:Yield only to traffic on your left.,d:Are traveling in the wrong direction.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop; yield to traffic and pedestrians and proceed when safe.

question: When driving in a work zone, what should you do about following distance?
options: a:Follow the vehicle ahead more closely to keep traffic moving.,b:Avoid tailgating and increase your following distance.,c:Maintain the exact same distance as on open roads.,d:Pass other vehicles as soon as you can.
note: In work zones, increase your following distance to allow extra stopping time and reduce the chance of collisions with workers or equipment.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are generally which color background?
options: a:White.,b:Yellow.,c:Green.,d:Blue.
note: Regulatory signs (speed limits, stop, yield, etc.) commonly use a white background with black or red letters/symbols and indicate laws that must be obeyed.

question: Which message appears on a red, octagonal sign?
options: a:Do not enter.,b:Stop.,c:One-way.
note: An eight-sided red sign always denotes STOP; you must come to a complete stop at that sign.

question: When should you not use your horn?
options: a:If you might hit another vehicle.,b:When visibility ahead is limited.,c:Near blind pedestrians.
note: Avoid using your horn near blind pedestrians; they rely on hearing and unexpected horns can be dangerous; yield instead.

question: When properly adjusted, what should your inside rearview mirror show?
options: a:Your own reflection.,b:Only the backseat passengers.,c:The entire rear window.,d:The front of your vehicle.
note: Position the inside rearview mirror so you can see the entire rear window from the driver's seat with only eye movement.

question: When should you allow extra following distance behind another vehicle?
options: a:When following a small passenger car.,b:When following a station wagon only.,c:When following a vehicle that cannot see behind it
note: Large vehicles and those towing trailers may have limited rear visibility; increase following distance to avoid collisions and to see past them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In traffic moving 50–55 mph, when are you least likely to have an accident?
options: a:When you drive several mph faster than most vehicles.,b:When you drive several mph slower than most vehicles.,c:When you travel within that same speed range as other vehicles.
note: Traveling at a similar speed to surrounding traffic (within limits) reduces speed differentials and lowers crash risk.

question: What does a green arrow signal require of drivers?
options: a:Yield only to pedestrians in the intersection.,b:Wait a set number of seconds before moving.,c:Proceed in the arrow's direction after yielding to any vehicles
note: A green arrow gives the right to proceed in the arrow direction but you must first yield to any remaining traffic or pedestrians in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is a primary danger of excessive speed?
options: a:Saves time getting to your destination.,b:Increases the chance of severe injury or death.,c:Reduces tire wear.,d:Helps you maneuver around obstacles.
note: Driving at excessive speed is a common contributing factor in crashes and increases the likelihood of serious injury or death; it rarely saves meaningful time.

question: Which statement about work zones is correct?
options: a:Work zones have no special rules.",b:You must slow for designated Cone Zones" and expect higher fines.,c:Slow only if you think workers are present.,d:Fines are the same as for normal driving and only slow when workers are visible.
note: Drive cautiously through work zones, obey posted speed limits and Slow for the Cone Zone signs; fines and penalties may be increased to protect workers.

question: Which behavior might identify an aggressive driver?
options: a:Driving under the posted speed limit.,b:Having many passengers in the vehicle.,c:Erratic and improper lane changes.
note: Aggressive drivers often make sudden or improper lane changes; stay out of their way to reduce risk.

question: For best control when turning quickly, how should your hands be positioned on the steering wheel?
options: a:Next to each other at the top of the wheel.,b:One hand at the top and one at the bottom.,c:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
note: Place both hands on opposite sides of the wheel (commonly near 9 and 3 or 8 and 4) for comfortable, safe steering and better control at higher speeds.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what is the safest action to take?
options: a:Glance toward the right edge of the road until the vehicle passes.,b:Switch to your high beams to judge distance.,c:Turn your lights on and off to get their attention.,d:Close your eyes briefly until the glare passes.
note: If an oncoming vehicle’s lights are dazzling you, look toward the right road edge instead of directly ahead to keep your vehicle safely on the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement is true about driving too slowly?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,b:The speed you drive has no effect on safety.,c:Driving too slowly is never unsafe.
note: Driving excessively slowly can be hazardous because it disrupts traffic flow and can provoke unsafe passing maneuvers.

question: In which situation should your wheels not be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,b:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,c:When parked on the side of a level roadway with no curb.,d:When stopped at a red light.
note: When parked facing uphill or downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or edge as appropriate to prevent rolling into traffic.

question: If you feel fatigued while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Increase the radio volume to stay alert.,b:Increase your speed to reach your destination faster.,c:Find a safe place to pull over and take a short nap.
note: If you are drowsy, stop in a safe area and rest or nap briefly; fatigue greatly increases crash risk.

question: When you want to change lanes, which action should you never do?
options: a:Signal well before changing lanes.,b:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,c:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,d:Move into another lane while within an intersection.
note: Never change lanes while inside an intersection; always check mirrors and blind spots and signal early.

question: What should you do when you encounter a deep puddle on the roadway?
options: a:Maintain the posted speed to drive through it.,b:Shift into neutral before entering the puddle.,c:Avoid the puddle if possible.
note: Avoid deep puddles when you can; water can hide hazards and increase the risk of hydroplaning and loss of control.

question: If your vehicle is struck from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Pressing your head against the headrest.,b:Be ready to apply brakes and keep a firm grip on the wheel.,c:Letting go of the steering wheel.
note: If hit from the rear, do not let go of the wheel. Press your head against the head restraint and maintain control so you can avoid further collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when should you move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:As soon as you feel like it.,c:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.,d:When you are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: Only return to your lane when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror and it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer signals you to stop despite a green traffic light, what must you do?
options: a:Obey the officer’s directions.,b:Follow the traffic signal instead of the officer.,c:Ignore both and proceed with caution.,d:Do what the vehicle ahead of you does.
note: A police officer’s instructions take precedence over traffic signals and signs; obey their directions.

question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver yourself?
options: a:Relax,b:Tailgate slower drivers to encourage them to speed up.,c:Drive above the posted limit to keep up with traffic.
note: Stay calm, concentrate on safe driving, give yourself enough travel time, and be forgiving of other drivers to avoid aggression.

question: Only which factor can reduce BAC and alcohol’s effects on the body?
options: a:Time for the body to eliminate alcohol.,b:Taking vitamin supplements.,c:Eating fatty foods before driving.,d:Drinking caffeinated beverages.
note: Only time allows your body to metabolize and lower blood alcohol concentration; other methods are ineffective.

question: When should drivers set the parking brake?
options: a:Only in parking lots.,b:Only when parked on a steep hill.,c:Every time they park.
note: Always set the parking brake when you park. Also leave a manual transmission in gear or an automatic in Park.

question: A broken yellow line down the center of the road signals what?
options: a:A construction zone ahead.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from either direction.
note: Broken yellow centerlines mean passing is allowed for traffic on either side when it is safe and clear of oncoming vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Into the second lane always.,b:Into any lane if it is safe.,c:Into the first available lane of the one-way street.
note: Turn from the lane nearest the centerline into the first legal lane of the one-way street you are entering.

question: If your vehicle becomes disabled on the highway, where should you park if possible?
options: a:Stop in the travel lane where you broke down.,b:Stop in the right lane and leave hazards off.,c:Park on any nearby shoulder even if partly blocking traffic.,d:With all four wheels off the traveled portion of the roadway.
note: If possible, remove your vehicle completely off the main-traveled portion of the road to reduce danger to you and other drivers.

question: Why is night driving more hazardous?
options: a:Distance and speed are harder to judge in the dark.,b:There are always fewer cars on the road at night.,c:Vehicles travel faster at night.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it difficult to judge distances and the speeds of other vehicles; you can only see as far as your headlights illuminate.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When it may help prevent a collision.,b:When you are angry at another driver.,c:To get other drivers moving in a traffic jam.
note: Use your horn only to alert others to avoid a collision or to warn of danger; not to express frustration.

question: For drivers under 21, a blood alcohol concentration of what level can lead to license suspension?
options: a:0.08 percent or higher.,b:Any detectable amount of alcohol.,c:0.15 percent or higher.
note: South Dakota has zero tolerance for drivers under 21; any detectable alcohol can result in penalties including a two-year license suspension.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers only.
note: Use low beams in fog; high beams can reflect back and worsen visibility, while four-way flashers do not improve forward vision.

question: If no crosswalk is present and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and allow the pedestrian to finish crossing.,b:Honk and continue slowly.,c:Ensure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.,d:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in the roadway even when there is no marked crosswalk; stop and let them cross.

question: What term describes the amount of alcohol in a person's blood?
options: a:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).,b:Implied consent (IC).,c:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).
note: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in the bloodstream; higher BAC means more impairment.

question: Tailgating (driving too close to the rear bumper ahead) can:
options: a:Never result in a traffic citation.,b:Frustrate other drivers and lead to unsafe behavior.,c:Reduce collisions by preventing cars from cutting in.
note: Tailgating can provoke aggressive reactions and lead to collisions; it can also result in citations for following too closely.

question: How far ahead should you be scanning the roadway while driving to avoid sudden maneuvers?
options: a:About ten seconds ahead.,b:About four seconds ahead.,c:About seven seconds ahead.
note: Look down the road roughly 10 seconds ahead to anticipate slowdowns, lane changes, and hazards, helping to avoid sudden braking.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim headlights, where should you look?
options: a:Directly at the approaching headlights so you can judge distance.,b:Toward the center line to maintain course.,c:Down at your dashboard until they pass.,d:Toward the right side of the road to avoid glare.
note: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded; this helps you stay on course without being dazzled by the other driver’s lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you avoid entering an intersection even if the light is green?
options: a:Only if you entered on a yellow light earlier.,b:If police are directing traffic elsewhere.,c:If you know you will block the intersection when the light turns red.,d:You may enter as long as the light is green regardless of congestion.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely; blocking the intersection is an offense even on green.

question: As you approach the crest of a hill, how should you prepare?
options: a:Maintain the same speed regardless of visibility.,b:Be prepared to stop if necessary and reduce speed as needed.,c:Speed up slightly to clear the hill faster.
note: You may not see hazards over the hill crest; adjust speed so you can stop if there's an obstruction or stalled vehicle ahead.

question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with vehicle speed?
options: a:Crash severity decreases as speed increases because of momentum.,b:Both stopping distance and crash severity increase as speed increases.,c:Speed has no effect on stopping distance or crash severity.,d:Stopping distance decreases with speed.
note: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more severe crashes due to greater energy in a collision.

question: A broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic means:
options: a:Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.,b:Passing is not permitted.,c:Passing is permitted when it's safe.,d:The lane is for buses only.
note: A dashed yellow centerline indicates passing is allowed when it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present.

question: When passing another vehicle, what is the recommended approach?
options: a:Honk continuously while passing to warn them.,b:Pass as safely and as quickly as possible then return when clear.,c:Match the other vehicle’s speed and stay alongside for several seconds.,d:Pass as slowly as possible to reduce noise.
note: Pass efficiently and safely to minimize the time spent out of your lane, returning only when it is safe to do so.

question: On an interstate, how can you best avoid vehicles merging from on-ramps to your right?
options: a:Change lanes to the left when traffic permits.,b:Maintain your current speed and position in the right lane.,c:Slow down in your lane so merging cars have space.
note: If traffic allows, move to the left lane to allow merging vehicles to enter safely from the right.

question: How can you encourage the driver behind you to keep a safe distance?
options: a:Brake abruptly to create space.,b:Maintain a steady speed.,c:Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,d:Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
note: Keep a steady speed and signal early for maneuvers to help drivers behind maintain a safe following distance.

question: How should you make room for vehicles entering a freeway?
options: a:Speed up to pass the merging vehicle quickly.,b:Maintain your speed and position without yielding.,c:Stop on the shoulder to let them in.,d:Change lanes or adjust your speed to allow them to merge.
note: If safe, merge to another lane or slow down slightly to create a gap for entering vehicles so they can join traffic smoothly.

question: Why should you leave extra following distance behind large vehicles?
options: a:Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before passing.,b:Because it keeps you from being caught in the vehicle’s slipstream.,c:To better see around the vehicle and because the driver may not see you.
note: Large vehicles can block your view of the road ahead and their drivers may not see you; increasing distance improves your visibility and safety.

question: What are work zone or construction signs usually like in appearance?
options: a:Square or rectangular with white background and red symbols.,b:Round or octagonal with black and yellow markings.,c:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with an orange background and black symbols.
note: Temporary construction and work zone signs use an orange background with black letters or symbols to warn drivers of work areas.

question: When a school bus has red flashing lights, when may vehicles proceed?
options: a:As soon as all students are off the bus.,b:When the stop arm is retracted but the bus remains stopped.,c:Only after the bus's red lights are off
note: Motorists must remain stopped until the bus turns off its red lights, retracts its stop arm, and starts moving again to ensure student safety.

question: If your car begins to skid, what should you avoid doing with the brakes?
options: a:Pump the brakes repeatedly.,b:Apply the brakes lightly.,c:Stay off the brakes.
note: When you skid, avoid braking; instead, steer smoothly to recover traction and control the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a roadway marked with a single broken white centerline, what is allowed?
options: a:You must stay in your lane and never cross.,b:You may cross the line to change lanes when safe.,c:You may change lanes only from the left lane.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes going the same direction and may be crossed when it is safe to change lanes or pass.

question: If stopped for a traffic violation, which documents must you present?
options: a:Only your license.,b:Only your insurance and registration.,c:Your driver's license
note: When stopped, you must produce your driver's license, current vehicle registration, and proof of insurance.

question: You park downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way do you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Toward the side of the road (right).,b:Toward the center of the road (left).,c:Straight ahead.
note: When parked downhill without a curb, turn the wheels toward the edge of the road so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if it moves.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips along the roadway?
options: a:To test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,b:To alert drivers to potential tire problems.,c:To warn inattentive drivers through vibration and sound that they are leaving the travel lane.,d:To provide extra traction in wet weather.
note: Rumble strips create vibration and noise to alert drivers who are drifting off the road or approaching hazards.

question: Which of these factors affects how alcohol is absorbed by an individual?
options: a:Intelligence.,b:Weight.,c:Height.,d:Clothing color.
note: Alcohol absorption is influenced by body weight, biological sex, amount of food in the stomach, and how much was consumed; only time removes alcohol from the system.

question: When may you legally drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:When you can see clearly both directions.,b:When warning lights are not flashing.,c:Never.
note: Do not go around or under any lowered railroad gate; wait until the gate is fully raised and it is safe to cross.

question: When passing a row of parked vehicles, what should you be prepared for?
options: a:All other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.,b:A person or vehicle unexpectedly entering your lane.,c:That it is safe to hug the parked vehicles to allow more traffic space.,d:To keep speed constant and maintain distance.
note: Leave space and be prepared for pedestrians or a vehicle suddenly emerging from between parked cars.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, which lane should you start from?
options: a:The center lane of the road.,b:Any lane as long as it’s safe.,c:The lane closest to the left curb.
note: When turning left from a one-way street to a one-way street, start from the far left lane and turn into the leftmost lane of the street you enter.

question: On a dimly lit street at night, what speed should you choose?
options: a:Keep instrument panel lights bright to be more visible.,b:Drive at the posted speed regardless of visibility.,c:Slow enough to stop within the distance illuminated by your headlights.,d:Use high beams so you can see farther without slowing.
note: At night you must drive at a speed that allows you to stop within the area lighted by your headlights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another car, when do you have enough room to return to your lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:After you look over your shoulder once.,c:When the other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.
note: Only re-enter your lane when you can clearly see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror indicating a safe gap.

question: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a minimum BAC of:
options: a:0.10 percent.,b:0.05 percent.,c:0.02 percent.,d:0.08 percent.
note: South Dakota law sets the legal blood alcohol concentration limit at 0.08% for drivers age 21 and over.

question: Truck blind spots are located:
options: a:On the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the truck.,b:Only on the immediate left of the cab.,c:Directly behind the truck only.
note: Trucks have large blind spots on the sides and directly behind; if you cannot see the truck driver’s face in their mirror, they probably cannot see you.

question: If pedestrians are crossing imprope rly (not in a crosswalk), what must you do?
options: a:You must stop for them.,b:You do not have to stop for them.,c:Honk your horn to make them move.,d:Drive around them carefully.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians whenever they are in the roadway, even if they are not in a marked crosswalk.

question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, which headlight setting is appropriate?
options: a:Keep your headlights on low beam so you don’t blind the driver ahead.,b:Use high beams until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.,c:Turn off your lights to be less distracting.,d:Use fog lights only.
note: Use low beams when following another vehicle to avoid dazzling the driver ahead and to reduce glare.

question: Which statement about large trucks is correct?
options: a:Large trucks are more maneuverable than passenger cars.,b:Large trucks require more distance to stop than passenger vehicles.,c:Large trucks are exempt from traffic laws regarding stopping distances.,d:All large trucks have brakes that allow quick stops similar to cars.
note: Due to size and weight, large trucks need considerably more distance to stop than passenger vehicles traveling at the same speed.

question: When making a left turn, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Signaling to other drivers.,b:Cutting the corner.,c:Slowing down before the turn.
note: Slow and signal before turning left, and avoid cutting the corner which can interfere with oncoming or adjacent traffic.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors while driving?
options: a:Often,b:Only when you want to check a blind spot.,c:Only when you are slowing down.
note: Make frequent mirror checks to stay aware of vehicles behind you and how traffic is moving; avoid a fixed stare ahead.

question: What does a curb painted red indicate?
options: a:The area is reserved for quick pick-up or drop-off.,b:No parking,c:Loading zone only.
note: A red curb means you may not stop, stand, or park there for any reason.

question: Driving significantly slower than surrounding traffic is generally:
options: a:A good idea if the weather is bad.,b:Often a hazard because it may cause others to pass unsafely.,c:Appropriate if you don’t know the speed limit.
note: Driving much slower than the flow can frustrate other drivers and increase the risk of being passed unsafely; match traffic speed within limits and conditions.

question: How many alcoholic drinks are enough to impair your driving ability?
options: a:Three drinks are needed to affect you.,b:Two drinks are required before impairment.,c:One drink can affect your driving.
note: Even a single alcoholic drink can impair judgment and reaction time; it's unsafe to drive after drinking any amount.

question: If another vehicle cuts in front of you dangerously close, what is the best immediate action?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas to increase space.,b:Honk and brake hard.,c:Swerve into the adjacent lane suddenly.
note: Removing your foot from the accelerator slows you and increases space without abrupt braking or risky maneuvers.

question: To reduce the chance of hydroplaning during rain, you should:
options: a:Put on cruise control to maintain speed.,b:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts raining.,c:Decrease your speed.
note: Lower your speed in wet conditions to reduce the risk of tires losing contact with the road surface and hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, when may you turn left onto another one-way street?
options: a:Only if traffic moves to the right on the street you're entering.,b:If you increase your speed before the turn.,c:When traffic on the street you are turning onto moves to the left.
note: You may turn left from a one-way onto another one-way street only if traffic on that street moves to the left and no sign forbids it.

question: When a red light is displayed but a green arrow points the way, when may you proceed?
options: a:Only after coming to a complete stop first.,b:Only after the red light changes to green.,c:If you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.
